content.rendered:
In the upper room, on the night before the cross, Jesus rose from supper, laid aside His outer garments, tied a towel around His waist, and washed the feet of the men who would abandon Him within hours. Then He gave them the commandment that would define Christian community for two thousand years.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, September 22, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another.”
John 13:34-35 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In the upper room in Jerusalem, on the night before the cross, Jesus rose from supper. He laid aside His outer garments. He tied a towel around His waist. He poured water into a basin. And He began to move around the room, kneeling before each disciple, washing the dust of the day off their feet. This was the work of the lowest household slave. It was the work no rabbi in Israel would have done for his followers. Yet the Master, the Teacher, the Lord, was doing it, one man at a time. Peter tried to stop Him. The other disciples watched in confused silence. When He was finished, He put His outer garments back on, returned to His place at the table, and looked at the twelve. Then He gave them the commandment that would define Christian community for two thousand years.

“A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another.” Two days ago we heard the greatest commandment. Love God. Yesterday we heard the second. Love your neighbour. Today Jesus goes further. To His disciples, the ones inside the covenant, He gives a new commandment. Not merely love one another. Love one another as I have loved you. The measuring rod for love in the church is not human affection. It is the love of Christ Himself, freshly demonstrated by the towel, the basin, and, within hours, the cross.

The Passion Translation opens up the intimacy of the moment: “So I give you now a new commandment: Love each other just as much as I have loved you. For when you demonstrate the same love I have for you by loving one another, everyone will know that you’re my true followers” (John 13:34-35 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I give you a new commandment: that you should love one another. Just as I have loved you, so you too should love one another. By this shall all [men] know that you are My disciples, if you love one another [if you keep on showing love among yourselves]” (John 13:34-35 AMPC). If you keep on showing love. Not a one-off gesture. A sustained way of life inside the family of God.

What makes this commandment “new” is not the general call to love. The Old Testament had already commanded love of neighbour. What is new is the standard. As I have loved you. The love the disciples had just watched. The love that took the towel. The love that would take the cross the next day. That is the love Jesus places on the church as the internal law of the family. And notice the outcome Jesus attaches. By this all will know. Not by our doctrinal precision. Not by our worship style. Not by our building programmes. By this, by love that mirrors the love of Christ, the watching world will know we are His disciples.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, look around your church, your small group, your circle of believing brothers and sisters. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, these are the ones Jesus is calling you to love as He has loved you. With the towel of humility. With the sustained kindness of the long haul. With forgiveness that keeps offering itself. With the willingness to lay down what you would rather hold. The watching world is looking for evidence. Let today be a day the evidence is visible.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has given the church the commandment to love one another as He has loved us. Not less. Not softer. Not on our own terms. As He has loved us. Today I choose to love my brothers and sisters in Christ with the humility of the towel and the persistence of the cross. I refuse to let bitterness settle. I refuse to withhold forgiveness. I refuse to hold offence against a fellow believer. The love You have poured into me in Christ, I pour out today. Let the world see. Let the world know. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I love my brothers and sisters in Christ as Jesus has loved me. Humbly. Persistently. Forgivingly. By this the world will know I am His disciple.
